items.question: Which 10 customers spent the most in total?
gold_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name,
       c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name,
       SUM(p.amount) AS total_spent
FROM customer c
JOIN payment p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id
ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.customer_id
LIMIT 10
items.notes: The README screenshot answered this wrongly (Marion, $64.87). True top: Karl Seal, $221.55.

items.question: What are the top 10 film categories by total revenue?

SELECT cat.category_id, cat.name AS category, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue
FROM payment p
JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id
JOIN category cat ON cat.category_id = fc.category_id
GROUP BY cat.category_id
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10

items.question: How many rentals happened each month?
gold_sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', rental_date)::date AS month, COUNT(*) AS rentals
FROM rental
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT m::date AS month, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rentals
FROM generate_series((SELECT date_trunc('month', MIN(rental_date)) FROM rental),
                     (SELECT date_trunc('month', MAX(rental_date)) FROM rental),
                     interval '1 month') AS m
LEFT JOIN rental r ON date_trunc('month', r.rental_date) = m
GROUP BY m
ORDER BY m
items.notes: Rentals run Feb–Aug 2022 with no rentals in Mar–Apr; listing those months as 0 is also accepted.

items.question: Which tables contain payment information?
Compare average rental duration by film category.

interpretations.label: Allowed rental period (film.rental_duration)
gold_sql:
SELECT cat.name AS category, AVG(f.rental_duration) AS avg_days
FROM film f
JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN category cat ON cat.category_id = fc.category_id
GROUP BY cat.name

interpretations.label: Actual time kept (return_date - rental_date)
gold_sql:
SELECT cat.name AS category,
       AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.return_date - r.rental_date)) / 86400) AS avg_days
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
JOIN film_category fc ON fc.film_id = i.film_id
JOIN category cat ON cat.category_id = fc.category_id
WHERE r.return_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cat.name

items.notes: 'Rental duration' can mean the allowed period on the film or how long customers actually kept it.

items.question: Which 10 customers generated the most revenue?
gold_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name AS customer_name, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id
ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.customer_id
LIMIT 10
items.notes: Revenue = payments.amount (equals order-item value net of discounts for non-cancelled orders). Counting cancelled orders is wrong.

items.question: What are the top 5 product categories by revenue?
gold_sql:
SELECT cat.category_id, cat.category_name AS category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - oi.discount_amount) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products pr ON pr.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN categories cat ON cat.category_id = pr.category_id
WHERE o.order_status <> 'cancelled'
GROUP BY cat.category_id
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5

SELECT cat.category_id, cat.category_name AS category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products pr ON pr.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN categories cat ON cat.category_id = pr.category_id
WHERE o.order_status <> 'cancelled'
GROUP BY cat.category_id
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
items.notes: Net (after discounts) and gross item value both accepted; cancelled orders must be excluded.

items.question: Using each product's preferred supplier cost, which 3 products have the biggest gap between list price and cost?
gold_sql:
SELECT pr.product_id, pr.product_name, pr.list_price - ps.unit_cost AS margin
FROM products pr
JOIN product_suppliers ps ON ps.product_id = pr.product_id AND ps.preferred_supplier
ORDER BY margin DESC, pr.product_id
LIMIT 3
items.notes: Shows that a cost question IS answerable here (unlike Pagila), when the cost data exists.
